additional_concerns: The legacy exclusions in node.1bf6918f69c6b37738daeb83, node.4e6a162c35678e9ddf17ad8e, node.ce439b1cf9ed8301fbb68f94 and node.ea4d19630f8cab09065b1909 implement declared assumptions. The source expressly preserves application processing but does not resolve whether that entails substantive unavailability of relief. Neither equivalence nor incompatibility is established without the relevant FAQs and existing-process rules.

Node.4d548f2e09bc36ef51212f64 excludes legacy applications from its question's scope; OUT_OF_SCOPE must not be treated as substantive disqualification. Node.b66b3e831bb98a12db59dffa tests substantive conditions without determining actual procedural relief.

The introduction refers to immediate effect, while the implementation provision specifies 28 November 2025 for measures in the FAQs. The specific date supports the proposed commencement assumption, but does not establish the legally decisive event for every implementation or transition scenario.

A fixed historical pending-status exclusion does not resolve subsequent approval, withdrawal or resubmission. The applicable SFC FAQs and existing approval or authorisation rules are missing; neither supplied unbound dependency ID can be reliably mapped to those authorities.

Item (ii) does not expressly add the separate home-supervision condition found in item (i). Home compliance, materiality, novelty, complexity and possible local policy implications remain supplied classifications; applying them to an actual change requires applicable home-jurisdiction rules and relevant interpretive guidance.
No formula establishes notification, filing or post-vetting compliance, legal approval, or an independent approval duty when relief is unavailable.
